title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is a complex-analytic curve (Riemann surface). P_X is the sheaf of étale (locally biholomorphic) maps X → P^1(C), i.e. local projective coordinates. H = Aut P^1 = PGL(2,C) acts on P_X by post-composition. On the previous page Grothendieck defined a pairing G (here written C): P_X × P_X → ω_X^{⊗2}. It is given by C(t,s) = (−2 s'''/s' + 3(s''/s')^2) dt^2, with derivatives taken with respect to t. This equals −2{s,t}dt^2, where {s,t} is the Schwarzian derivative of s with respect to t. He proved two properties: (I) invariance under H×H; (II) the cocycle identity C(t,s)+C(s,r)=C(t,r), hence C(t,t)=0 and antisymmetry.

This page adds the converse statements (III), which come from ODE theory.
(a) On a connected open U, C(t,s)=0 implies s = g·t for some g ∈ H. This is the classical fact that the Schwarzian vanishes exactly on Möbius transformations.
(b) For a fixed coordinate t, the map s ↦ C(t,s) induces an injection H\P_X → ω_X^{⊗2}, injective by (a). It is also surjective, because any local quadratic differential is locally a Schwarzian: take a ratio of two independent solutions of y'' + (q/4)y = 0 or similar. So H\P_X ≅ ω_X^{⊗2} once t is chosen.

Next he makes this intrinsic. A Proposition, 'almost formal from (II)', states that there is an ω^{⊗2}-torsor Conn_X, unique up to unique isomorphism, with an H-invariant map c^X: P_X → Conn_X, t ↦ c_t, such that C(t,s) = c_s − c_t. Conn_X is the torsor built from the cocycle by gluing; equivalently it is the quotient of P_X × ω^{⊗2} by the cocycle relation. It is named the sheaf of (holomorphic) projective connections on X, and c^X induces a canonical isomorphism H\P_X ≅ Conn_X.

Finally, functoriality: an étale map f: X' → X gives P_{X'} ≅ f^{-1}P_X and Conn_{X'} ≅ f^{-1}Conn_X, with c^{X'} and f^{-1}c^X compatible.

The next page notes that P^1 carries a unique projective connection, since H^0(P^1, ω^{⊗2}) = 0. It shows c_t = t^*(canonical connection) and then extends the whole construction to relative curves X/S, using étale maps to P^1_S and principal parts of order ≤ 3.

Purpose within the file (Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs / Cartier operator): to set up an intrinsic, algebraizable notion of projective connection (Schwarzian structure) on curves. The likely aim is a relative and characteristic-p theory alongside Picard–Fuchs equations and the Cartier operator.
errors: No substantive errors. With the normalization C(t,s) = −2{s,t}dt^2, the cocycle identity C(t,s)+C(s,r) = C(t,r) follows from the Schwarzian chain rule. Invariance under Möbius transformations in either argument also checks out.
III a) needs U connected; Grothendieck added this in the margin.
Writing C(t,s) = c_s − c_t, rather than c_t − c_s, is consistent with (II): c_s−c_t + c_r−c_s = c_r−c_t.

Minor: the quotient H\P_X is a quotient sheaf. The iso H\P_X ≅ ω^{⊗2} depends on t, while H\P_X ≅ Conn_X is canonical, as he says. Conn_X is locally trivial; global sections exist on compact curves (e.g. by uniformization, or since H^1(X, ω^{⊗2}) = 0 for g ≥ 2), but not canonically.

ideas.what: The Schwarzian derivative viewed as a 1-cocycle on the sheaf of local projective coordinates with values in quadratic differentials, invariant under PGL2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schwarz, Kummer, Cartan; sheaf-theoretic formulation by Gunning (1966-67)

ideas.what: Converse: vanishing Schwarzian characterizes Möbius-related coordinates, and every local quadratic differential is a Schwarzian (existence via 2nd-order linear ODE)
ideas.modern_name: Schwarzian equation / correspondence between projective structures and Sturm-Liouville operators

ideas.what: Sheaf of projective connections Conn_X as an ω^{⊗2}-torsor obtained formally from the cocycle, with a canonical isomorphism H\P_X ≅ Conn_X, compatible with étale pullback
ideas.modern_name: torsor of projective connections (affine space over H^0(ω^2)); opers for PGL2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning; algebraic/relative form Deligne (1970s), Mochizuki (indigenous bundles, 1996), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers)

ideas.what: Unique projective connection on P^1, and c_t = t^*(canonical) (next page)

missed.claim: In a file on Gauss–Manin, Picard–Fuchs and the Cartier operator, Grothendieck sets up projective connections intrinsically, as an ω^{⊗2}-torsor defined via étale maps to P^1. On the next page he extends this to relative curves over arbitrary bases. This suggests an early (c. 1972) intent to study projective connections and Schwarzian equations in characteristic p together with the Cartier operator and p-curvature. That theme was later developed by Ihara (Schwarzian equations in char p, mid-1970s) and Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory, indigenous bundles), apparently without reference to these notes.
missed.quote: Le faisceau Conn_X est appelé le faisceau des connexions projectives (analytiques complexes) sur X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's early engagement with projective connections in an arithmetic and de Rham context. The mathematics on this page itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, sheaf-theoretic rederivation of classical facts: the Schwarzian cocycle, the torsor of projective connections, and H\P_X ≅ Conn_X. Mainly its context in a Cartier-operator and Picard–Fuchs file is mildly interesting historically.
transcription_corrections: The pairing is written G(t,s) in the image (consistent with the previous page), not C(t,s). The boxed formula reads G(t,s) = c_s − c_t.
'Proposition (presque formelle à partir de (II))': the reference is to condition (II), the cocycle identity.
'Un morphisme étale f: X' → X' begins the functoriality paragraph. It is not part of the line 'c^X : H\P_X ≅ Conn_X'.
In III b) the struck-out text is 'P_X/H' and the margin remark reads 'd'après a)'.
